title: Jonas Salk: 112 Years Ago Today, the Man Who Beat Polio and Gave It Away

lines: He beat polio, and refused to patent it.
Who changed the world today? October 28.
Who changed the world today? October twenty-eighth.
112 years ago today, a boy was born in New York City.
A hundred and twelve years ago today, a boy was born in New York City.
His name: Jonas Salk.

lines: He was the first in his family to go to college.
After medical school, he skipped treating patients to study viruses.
In 1947, he got his own virus lab in Pittsburgh.
In nineteen forty-seven, he got his own virus lab in Pittsburgh.
Back then, polio was every parent's nightmare.
Each summer, pools closed and children were kept inside.
In 1952, the US had about 58,000 cases.
In nineteen fifty-two, the U.S. had about fifty-eight thousand cases.
More than 3,000 people died.
More than three thousand people died.
Many children could never walk again.
Some could only breathe inside an iron lung.
Salk made a vaccine from killed virus.
In 1953, he even gave it to his own children.
In nineteen fifty-three, he even gave it to his own children.

In nineteen fifty-four, more than a million children
joined the largest vaccine trial in history.

the vaccine was safe and effective.
A reporter asked who owned the patent.
Salk said: Well, the people, I would say.
There is no patent. Could you patent the sun?
In 1963, he founded the Salk Institute in California.
In nineteen sixty-three, he founded the Salk Institute in California.
He died in 1995, at the age of eighty.
He died in nineteen ninety-five, at the age of eighty.
Today, polio cases are down more than 99% since 1988.

His question for you:
if you made something that changed the world,
would you give it to everyone?
